name: Poland
traditionNote: A continental civil-law system in which the published text of the act governs: courts do not bind one another by precedent, though resolutions of the Supreme Court and the line of rulings of the Constitutional Tribunal carry weight that is hard to distinguish from it in practice.
summary: A statute (ustawa) is passed by the Sejm, considered by the Senat — which may propose amendments or reject the bill, and can be overridden by an absolute majority of the Sejm — and then signed by the President, who may instead veto it, sending it back for a three-fifths override, or refer it to the Constitutional Tribunal. It becomes law by promulgation in the Dziennik Ustaw, and under the Act of 20 July 2000 on the promulgation of normative acts it enters into force fourteen days after promulgation unless it provides otherwise. Since 1 January 2012 the Dziennik Ustaw and the Monitor Polski exist only in electronic form, and the day an act is promulgated is the day its electronic file appears on the issuing authority's website; each file is a signed PDF whose certificates the publisher lists separately. Executive rules take the form of rozporządzenia issued by the Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister or individual ministers on a specific statutory authorisation. Consolidated texts are not merely editorial in Poland: when a statute has been amended enough, the responsible authority announces a tekst jednolity by obwieszczenie in the Dziennik Ustaw, and that announced text is itself official.
hierarchy: Ratified international agreements consented to by statute, and EU law, which under Article 91 take precedence over statutes that cannot be reconciled with them
Ustawa — statutes of the Sejm, and rozporządzenia z mocą ustawy in the narrow martial-law case
Ratified agreements not requiring prior statutory consent
Rozporządzenie — regulations of the Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister and ministers, issued only on a specific statutory authorisation
Akty prawa miejscowego — local enactments of voivodeship, county and commune authorities, published in the voivodeship official journal
Uchwały and zarządzenia — resolutions and orders binding only the units subordinate to the body issuing them

gazette.name: Dziennik Ustaw
gazette.en: Journal of Laws of the Republic of Poland
gazette.authority: Prezes Rady Ministrów (Prime Minister), published with the assistance of Rządowe Centrum Legislacji
gazette.coverage: Continuous position numbering by year, back through the printed era; electronic-only publication since 1 January 2012
gazette.desc: Where a Polish statute becomes law. It carries statutes, regulations of the Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister and ministers, ratified international agreements, rulings of the Constitutional Tribunal, and the obwieszczenia that announce consolidated texts. Citation is by year and position — Dz.U. 2019 poz. 1461 — not by page.
gazette.howto: Enter a year and a position number in the 'Rok' and 'Pozycja' boxes and press 'Przejdź', or search by title. The front page lists the most recently promulgated items with their publication dates and files. Every item is a signed PDF; 'Lista certyfikatów' holds the certificates you need to verify those signatures, which is what makes the electronic file the authentic text rather than a copy of one.
gazette.note: The day of promulgation is the day the electronic file appears here — printed reproductions have no independent standing, and there has been no paper edition since 2012.

constitution.name: Konstytucja Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
constitution.native: Konstytucja Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej z dnia 2 kwietnia 1997 r.
constitution.en: Constitution of the Republic of Poland
constitution.authority: Adopted by the National Assembly and confirmed by referendum 25 May 1997; published as Dz.U. 1997 nr 78 poz. 483
constitution.coverage: In force since 17 October 1997, amended in 2006 and 2009
constitution.desc: A long post-communist constitution with an extensive rights chapter, a Constitutional Tribunal empowered to strike statutes down, and Article 91, which gives ratified agreements consented to by statute — and EU law — precedence over irreconcilable statutes.
constitution.howto: The ISAP record gives the promulgated text as a PDF together with its amendments and related acts. The Sejm publishes an English translation at sejm.gov.pl/prawo/konst/angielski/kon1.htm, alongside German, French, Russian and Spanish versions.
constitution.note: Amendment requires a two-thirds Sejm majority and an absolute Senate majority; changes to chapters I, II or XII may additionally be put to a confirmatory referendum.

sources.name: Monitor Polski
sources.authority: Prezes Rady Ministrów, published with the assistance of Rządowe Centrum Legislacji
sources.coverage: Position numbering by year; electronic-only since 1 January 2012
sources.desc: The second official gazette, for instruments that are not sources of universally binding law: resolutions of the Sejm and the Senat, orders of the President and the Prime Minister, announcements, communications, and the notices — interest rates, indexation figures, tax thresholds — that a great deal of practice actually turns on.
sources.howto: Same interface as the Dziennik Ustaw: year plus position, or a title search. Citations take the form M.P. 2026 poz. 123.
sources.note: Nothing here creates universally binding law. If a rule affects citizens generally, it belongs in the Dziennik Ustaw, and if you find it only in the Monitor Polski, that is itself a fact about its standing.

sources.name: ISAP
sources.authority: Ośrodek Informatyki Kancelarii Sejmu (IT Centre of the Chancellery of the Sejm)
sources.coverage: Bibliographic records and texts of everything published in the Dziennik Ustaw and the Monitor Polski, from 1918 onward, including the acts of the Polish authorities in exile
sources.desc: The finding aid Polish lawyers actually start from. For each act it gives the promulgated text, the announced consolidated text where one exists, an editorially unified text, the status (in force, repealed, expired), the acts that amended it and the acts it amended, and the executive regulations issued under it.
sources.howto: Use 'Roczniki' to browse by year and publisher, 'Hasła' for the subject index, and 'Wyszukiwanie' for a search by title, year, position or keyword. On an act's page, distinguish the three text types: 'tekst ogłoszony' is what was promulgated, 'tekst jednolity' is the consolidated text officially announced by obwieszczenie, and 'tekst ujednolicony' is ISAP's own editorial merge, which is convenient and not official.
sources.note: The site sits behind a bot wall and may show an interstitial to anything that is not a browser; it is not down when that happens.

sources.name: ELI & Sejm API
sources.en: Open API for legal acts and parliamentary data
sources.coverage: Acts published in the Dziennik Ustaw and the Monitor Polski, addressed by ELI identifiers, plus Sejm data: members, prints, interpellations, committees, sittings and votes
sources.desc: Poland exposes its gazette through the European Legislation Identifier scheme, so an act has a stable machine address of the form eli/DU/2019/1461 and its text and metadata can be fetched rather than scraped.
sources.howto: Read the documentation page, which is in English and Polish, and build requests against the ELI endpoints for acts or the Sejm endpoints for parliamentary material; PDFs and structured metadata come back from the same identifiers used on the public sites.

sources.name: Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
sources.en: Sejm of the Republic of Poland
sources.coverage: The current term in full, with earlier terms archived term by term; bills (druki sejmowe), committee work, stenographic records and votes
sources.desc: Where a statute is followed while it is still a bill. The druk sejmowy — the numbered print of a bill — carries the explanatory memorandum (uzasadnienie) and the regulatory impact assessment, which are the standard materials for arguing what a provision was meant to do.
sources.howto: Work from the current term's pages to the process legislacyjny for a bill, following it by print number through readings, committee reports and Senate amendments; the same records are reachable programmatically through the Sejm API. Bills that fall at the end of a term are not carried over, so check the term as well as the number.
sources.note: The Senat's own site holds the Senate stage of the same bill, including its amendments and their fate.

sources.name: Senat Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
sources.en: Senate of the Republic of Poland
sources.coverage: Bills received from the Sejm, Senate amendments, committee opinions and sitting records, by term
sources.desc: The second chamber's file on a bill. It matters for legislative history because Senate amendments are voted on separately in the Sejm, so the final wording of a contested provision is often decided here rather than in the original bill.
sources.howto: Open the current term's legislative work, find the bill by its Senate print number or by title, and read the committee opinion and the resolution adopted; the Sejm record then shows whether each amendment was accepted or rejected.
sources.note: The site answers automated requests with 403 while serving browsers normally.

sources.name: Sad Najwyzszy
sources.coverage: The court's judgment database, the official reports (OSNC, OSNKW and the other series), legal questions referred to it, and its bulletins
sources.desc: The court of cassation for civil, criminal, labour and military matters. Its resolutions answering legal questions — especially those given the force of a legal principle — are not formally binding on other courts but are followed as if they were.
sources.howto: Search 'Baza orzeczeń' by case reference, date or keyword; 'Najnowsze orzeczenia' lists what has just been published, and 'Urzędowe zbiory orzeczeń' holds the official reports in which a decision's headnote is authoritative. 'Zagadnienia prawne' shows the legal questions pending, which is where a change in the case law is usually visible first.
sources.note: Case references have the form III CZP 12/25, where the roman numeral is the chamber; quoting the chamber matters, because the same number recurs across them.

sources.name: Portal Orzeczen Sadow Powszechnych
sources.en: Judgments portal of the common courts
sources.authority: Ministerstwo Sprawiedliwości (Ministry of Justice), publishing judgments supplied by the courts
sources.coverage: Selected judgments of the district, regional and appellate courts, with reasons, published progressively since the portal opened
sources.desc: First and second instance decisions, which is where most Polish litigation actually ends. Publication is selective — a court publishes what it considers of interest — so absence from the portal says nothing about a case.
sources.howto: Search by court, case reference, date range, subject or the provision applied; each judgment is anonymised and carries its reasons. The portal is a JavaScript application, so it needs a browser rather than a fetcher.
sources.note: Anonymisation removes names and identifying details, which occasionally removes the fact the case turned on.

sources.name: SAOS
sources.authority: A non-governmental project aggregating decisions published by the courts
sources.coverage: Judgments of the common courts, the Supreme Court, the administrative courts and the Constitutional Tribunal, gathered from their own publication systems
sources.desc: One search across court systems that do not share one, plus a documented API — which makes it the practical route to Polish case law in bulk, and a workable second route to decisions of courts whose own sites are hard to reach.
sources.howto: Use the search across all courts at once, filter by court type, date or judge, and take the 'Programowe API' section for machine access. Every record links back to the source system, which is where you should confirm the text before relying on it.
sources.note: Not an official publisher. Its holdings are only as complete and as current as what the courts publish, and it can lag.

sources.name: Elektroniczne Dzienniki Urzedowe
sources.authority: Each Wojewoda (voivode) publishes the journal for that voivodeship, on a shared platform
sources.coverage: Local enactments of the voivodeship, county and commune authorities, position-numbered by year, electronic since 2012
sources.desc: Local law in Poland — zoning plans, local taxes and fees, waste rules, statutes of communes — is promulgated in the official journal of the voivodeship, not in the Dziennik Ustaw, and takes effect fourteen days after that publication unless it says otherwise. There are sixteen such journals, one per voivodeship, each at its own address; this is the Lower Silesian one.
sources.howto: Find the journal for the voivodeship the commune belongs to, then search by title or use the advanced search by year, position, issuing body and date. A resolution of a commune council appears here under the commune's name, so the name of the place is usually the fastest key.
sources.note: Each voivodeship runs its own instance and some of them are unreachable from outside Poland; if one address does not answer, the enactment can often be found through the commune's own bulletin of public information (BIP).

sources.name: Internetowa Baza Traktatowa
sources.en: Treaty database of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.authority: Ministerstwo Spraw Zagranicznych (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
sources.coverage: Agreements to which Poland is or was a party, in force and expired, including some that went through the treaty procedure without being promulgated
sources.desc: Ratified agreements consented to by statute rank above ordinary statutes under Article 91 of the Constitution, so the treaty text is part of domestic law rather than background to it. The database gives the text together with its status and the instrument that brought it into force.
sources.howto: Search by party, title or date; the introduction explains the four categories the base covers, and warns that it does not hold every agreement Poland has ever concluded. Where an agreement was promulgated, the Dziennik Ustaw item is the authentic text.
sources.note: The base states openly that it is not exhaustive — absence from it is not evidence that no agreement exists.

sources.name: Constitution in English (Sejm)
sources.en: The Constitution of Poland in translation
sources.coverage: The full text of the 1997 Constitution in five languages
sources.desc: The Chancellery of the Sejm's own translations of the Constitution — the only substantial piece of Polish legislation translated by the state and kept in one predictable place.
sources.howto: Read it chapter by chapter from the index; the other language versions sit under the parallel paths for niemiecki, francuski, rosyjski and hiszpański.
sources.note: A translation, with no legal force. There is no official English text of Polish statutes generally — for those, the commercial services or nothing.

sources.name: EUR-Lex (po polsku)
sources.authority: Urząd Publikacji Unii Europejskiej (Publications Office of the European Union)
sources.coverage: EU treaties, legislation, consolidated texts, case law and national implementing measures, in Polish among the official languages
sources.desc: Article 91 puts EU law above irreconcilable Polish statutes, and regulations apply without any Polish act, so a search that stops at the Dziennik Ustaw is incomplete for anything within EU competence.
sources.howto: Search by CELEX number or subject with the interface set to Polish; the national implementing measures tab on a directive lists the Polish acts notified as implementing it.
sources.note: The Polish language version of an EU act is authentic alongside the others; the Official Journal edition is the binding one.

sources.name: LEX
sources.authority: Wolters Kluwer Polska, a private publisher
sources.coverage: Legislation with editorial consolidation, case law including unpublished decisions, commentaries, monographs and practice guidance
sources.desc: With Legalis, one of the two systems Polish practice actually runs on. It is worth naming precisely because so much Polish legal work happens inside a subscription product rather than on the free state sites.
sources.howto: Access requires a subscription or an institutional login; the free state sources above cover the texts themselves, and what a subscription buys is the annotation, the commentary and the unreported case law.
sources.note: Private and commercial. Its consolidated texts are editorial work — where the wording matters, go back to the Dziennik Ustaw item or the announced tekst jednolity.

findLaw.task: Find the current text of a statute
findLaw.steps: Search ISAP by title, open the act's record and take the most recent 'tekst jednolity' — the consolidated text officially announced by obwieszczenie in the Dziennik Ustaw — then check the list of amending acts underneath for anything published after it. ISAP's own 'tekst ujednolicony' is quicker but editorial.

findLaw.task: Read the act exactly as promulgated
findLaw.steps: Take the Dz.U. citation — year and position, as in Dz.U. 2019 poz. 1461 — and enter the two numbers in the 'Rok' and 'Pozycja' boxes on the Dziennik Ustaw site. The signed PDF that comes back is the authentic text; the certificate list on the same site is what lets you verify the signature.

findLaw.task: Work out what an amendment changed and when it bites
findLaw.steps: Open the amending act in the Dziennik Ustaw and read its final articles, which carry the entry-into-force and transitional provisions; the default is fourteen days after promulgation. ISAP's record for the amended act lists every amending act with its Dz.U. position, which is the fastest way to see the sequence.

For the Supreme Court, search the Baza orzeczeń by case reference including the chamber numeral. For district, regional and appellate judgments, use the Ministry of Justice judgments portal. To search across court systems at once, or to pull decisions in bulk, use SAOS and follow its link back to the source.
findLaw.source: Portal Orzeczeń Sądów Powszechnych / Sąd Najwyższy

findLaw.steps: Rulings of the Constitutional Tribunal are promulgated in the Dziennik Ustaw, so a ruling striking a provision down can be found there by year and position, and ISAP records it against the act it affected — including the date from which the provision lost force, which is often deferred. SAOS also carries the Tribunal's decisions.

Identify the voivodeship the commune lies in, open that voivodeship's official journal, and search by the commune's name or by year and position. Local enactments take effect fourteen days after publication there unless they provide otherwise; a resolution that was never published in the journal did not take effect.

findLaw.task: Follow a bill, or read why a provision was written
findLaw.steps: Find the druk sejmowy for the bill on the Sejm site and read the uzasadnienie attached to it, then follow the print through readings, committee reports and Senate amendments. The Sejm API exposes the same prints and proceedings for scripted work.

subnational: Poland is a unitary state with three tiers of local government — 16 voivodeships, some 380 counties and about 2,500 communes — none of which has legislative power in the sense of enacting statutes. What they issue are akty prawa miejscowego: local enactments, valid only within the unit's territory and only within powers granted by statute, covering zoning plans, local taxes and fees, waste and public order rules and the statutes of the units themselves. They are promulgated not in the Dziennik Ustaw but in the official journal of the voivodeship, published by the voivode, and enter into force fourteen days after that publication unless they provide otherwise. There are sixteen such journals on a shared electronic platform, each at its own address, and some are hard to reach from outside Poland; the commune's own bulletin of public information is the usual fallback. Resolutions that merely bind the administration internally are not local law and are not published there at all.
caveats: Poland distinguishes three kinds of text and the distinction is load-bearing: the tekst ogłoszony promulgated in the Dziennik Ustaw, the tekst jednolity announced officially by obwieszczenie, and the tekst ujednolicony that ISAP and the commercial systems merge editorially. Only the first two are official, and a consolidated text can be months behind the amendments made since it was announced. Rulings of the Constitutional Tribunal frequently defer the loss of force of the provision they strike down, so a provision may be unconstitutional and still binding on the date you are reading it. Several official sites — the Constitutional Tribunal, the administrative courts' judgment database, the Government Legislation Centre's drafts service — are unreachable from parts of the internet outside Poland, which is why they are described here rather than linked; SAOS is a workable second route to the case law, though it is not an official publisher. The English text of the Constitution is a translation and has no legal force, and there is no official English version of Polish statutes at all. Judgments in the common-courts portal are anonymised and published selectively; absence proves nothing.
